_readme: The identity-claim contract: what a client may honestly say about who someone is.
Derived from docs/IDENTITY-CLAIM-MATRIX.md (rulings 2026-08-10) and the settled copy in docs/COPY-AUDIT-2026-08-10.md §1.
This file is the single source for BOTH the state rules and the user-facing strings.
The Rust SDK and the JS SDK each load this file and must reproduce every vector exactly;
clients render what the SDK hands them and may append only platform affordance suffixes.
A copy change is a diff to this file and nothing else.
stamping_epoch: rows older than this read Unknown when they carry no account tag and their
sender is absent, because tag absence proves nothing before servers stamped tags. The code
landed 2026-06-27 (b8459976 account stamp, 14514790 origin persistence); both production
servers demonstrably stamped by 2026-08-01. A dated constant is a smell we accepted
knowingly: unlike legacy signatures, which announce themselves by their bare-base64 shape,
tag ABSENCE has no format to inspect, so the row's own timestamp is the only
wire-derivable discriminator. It lives here, once, and in no client.

atProtocol.label: AT Protocol identity
atProtocol.line: This is a real, self-owned identity. Its owner holds the key below and signs everything they send — so anyone can prove a message really came from them, on freeq or anywhere else on the network.

selfIssued.label: Self-issued identity
selfIssued.line: This is a self-issued identity, not tied to a Bluesky account. Its owner holds the key below and signs everything they send — so anyone can prove a message really came from them, on freeq or anywhere else on the network.

relayed.label: Relayed identity
relayed.line: Relayed from {origin}. This server didn't verify the sender's identity — {origin} vouches for it.

guest.label: Guest
guest.line_local: No account — just a nickname on this server. Nothing they send is signed.
guest.line_relayed: No account — just a nickname on {origin}. Nothing they send is signed.

unknown.label: Unknown
unknown.line: No identity information is attached to this name.

sender_vectors._comment: claim_for_sender: a person surface anchored to a message (profile sheet or popover opened from a row). Live identity first, then the message's own evidence, then the lookup machine. Differs from the row rule in exactly one place: a live-known DID outranks the row's tag, because this surface answers who the person is NOW.
